claims.text: Lightweight HEAs can combine low density, high mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
This combination of properties is enabled by a homogeneous, finely grained single-phase microstructure.
High mixing entropy stabilizes the single-phase microstructure.
Sluggish diffusion maintains the single-phase microstructure and promotes grain refinement.
The refined grain structure mechanically strengthens the alloy.
A homogeneous single-phase microstructure produces a uniform distribution of alloying elements.
Uniformly distributed alloying elements enable rapid formation of protective Al-rich and/or Cr-rich oxide scales.
The Al-rich and/or Cr-rich oxide scales are adherent and self-healing.
Reducing the concentration of a low-density alloying element can destabilize the microstructure.
Microstructural destabilization caused by compositional variation leads to intermetallic precipitation and/or grain coarsening.
Thermal exposure beyond a critical phase-stability limit leads to intermetallic precipitation and grain coarsening.
Intermetallic precipitation and/or grain coarsening reduce tensile strength relative to the baseline alloy.
Intermetallic precipitation and/or grain coarsening increase corrosion current density relative to the baseline alloy.
Intermetallic precipitation and/or grain coarsening increase oxidation mass gain relative to the baseline alloy.
Loss of microstructural stability causes the protective oxide mechanism to fail.
The baseline alloy exhibits the targeted combination of mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
